newsitem.title: USA: News Corp likely buyer of Dodgers team.
newsitem.headline: News Corp likely buyer of Dodgers team.

text.p: If News Corp Ltd winds up buying the Los Angeles Dodgers, it will be the latest in a line of corporations gobbling up professional sports teams to provide programming for cable television operations and add "brands" to the corporate roster.

Rather than sell the broadcast rights, a company can add team broadcasts to its own TV and radio properties. Tribune Co, owner of the Chicago Cubs baseball team, does that, as does Walt Disney Co, which owns the Anaheim Angels baseball team and the Mighty Ducks hockey team.
For Rupert Murdoch, who with his family controls News Corp, a purchase would be the latest step in his aggressive drive to create and acquire news and sports programming.

"It's really about controlling content," said Steve Barlow, an analyst who follows media companies for CS First Boston. "The benefit is that you get to control the distribution of your programming. It's also a way to complement a local presence in cable or broadcasting. You can add it to your regional sports channel, and it gives you some unique programming."
News Corp could add the Dodgers to its cable sports joint venture with Liberty Media Corp.
Analysts said that baseball is a particularly attractive broadcast property because it offers advertisers sought-after male viewers.
"That's a target audience that advertisers like," said Rita Zanella at Gruntal & Co. "There are very few programs out there that attractive to male viewers."
Owning a baseball team also offers strong merchandising outlets. "Merchandising is always important from the vantage of cross branding and cross promotion," said Zanella.

Analysts said that corporate ownership of a sports team can turn into more of a vanity purchase than a boost to the bottom line. They noted that the economics of baseball have especially soured after the baseball strike in 1994, with a downturn in fan and advertiser interest.
Barlow said that a potential purchase of the Dodgers was likely the tip of the iceberg for Murdoch. "I don't think the rest of the strategy has been revealed yet."
To date, the bulk of Murdoch's strategy has been via a national audience. The Fox Sports unit broadcast games from the National Football League, National Hockey League, and Major League Baseball.

"L.A. is obvious a huge market, and he can use it and program it anywhere else where he has satellite operations arond the world," said Barlow. News Corp has satellite TV operations in Asia, Britain and China.
The Dodgers said it has asked the Major League Baseball's Executive Council for permission to negotiate to sell the team to News Corp's Fox Sports unit.
Corporate ownership of sports teams includes: Time Warner Inc, which acquired the Atlanta Braves baseball team and the Atlanta Hawks basketball team when it bought Turner Broadcasting.
Cablevision Systems Corp last month bought the New York Rangers hockey team and the N.Y. Knicks basketball team.
Comcast Corp owns the Philadelphia Flyers hockey team and the Philadelphia 76ers basketball team.
Boston Celtics Lp, which owns the basketball team, and Florida Panthers, the hockey team, are both publicly owned.
